title: Day 83 · Week 11, Day 6 — Myths: she has to sleep on her left side from now on, pelvic floor training makes the birth harder, and sit-ups split her stomach muscles
summary: Three myths about the months ahead. Sleep: the vena cava compression is real in late pregnancy, and from 28 weeks going to sleep on the back was linked to 2.6 times the odds of late stillbirth (Cronin 2019 IPD meta-analysis, 851 cases, 2,257 controls) on a baseline of roughly 1–9 per 1,000 — but the right side is as safe as the left (aOR 1.04), and before 28–30 weeks a prospective cohort of 8,706 first pregnancies (nuMoM2b) found no link between back or right-side sleep and stillbirth, growth restriction or hypertensive disorders. Pelvic floor training: in 18,865 Norwegian first-time mothers, training three or more times a week did not increase severe tears, episiotomy, instrumental birth or emergency caesarean, and a meta-analysis of 12 trials found slightly shorter labour stages with no change in tears. Abdominal separation: present in 100% of first-time mothers at 35 weeks and 33% at 21 weeks, narrowing over the first year, not linked to back or pelvic pain; antenatal exercise associated with 35% less diastasis on weak evidence; curl-ups narrow rather than widen the gap. Why ACOG's advice on avoiding long periods supine during exercise is about blood flow, not abdominal muscles.
action: In the shared calendar, put one entry at 28 weeks (Day 196): 'Side-sleeping from tonight, either side. Pillows.' In the pregnancy file's Pelvic floor section, add: 'Every squeeze ends with a full let-go.' Tonight, tell her the short version: any sleep position she likes, for now.
